<!-- ===================================================================== -->
<!--  2. DRAW THE SAMPLE                                                   -->
<!--  The source file is ~11.6 GB / ~18 million rows, so it is never read  -->
<!--  into memory whole. We stream it once, keep each row with probability -->
<!--  p = SAMPLE_N / (estimated rows), keep only the columns we need, and  -->
<!--  cache the result. Later knits reuse the cache and are near-instant.  -->
<!-- ===================================================================== -->

```{r sample-data}
## Estimate the row count from the file size and the average bytes per row in
## the first 50 MB. Far cheaper than counting 18 million lines, and only needs
## to be accurate enough to set the sampling probability.
estimate_total_rows <- function(path, probe_bytes = 50e6) {
  size  <- file.info(path)$size
  con   <- file(path, "rb"); on.exit(close(con))
  probe <- readBin(con, "raw", n = min(probe_bytes, size))
  n_nl  <- sum(probe == as.raw(0x0a))
  if (n_nl == 0) stop("Could not find any line breaks in the probe.")
  floor(size / (length(probe) / n_nl))
}

## Method 1: let awk do the sampling before the data ever reaches R.
sample_with_awk <- function(path, p, keep_cols, seed) {
  cmd <- sprintf(
    "awk 'BEGIN{srand(%d)} NR==1 || rand()<%.10f' %s",
    seed, p, shQuote(path)
  )
  fread(
    cmd = cmd, select = keep_cols, stringsAsFactors = TRUE,
    check.names = FALSE, showProgress = TRUE
  )
}

## Method 2: pure R fallback (no shell tools; works on Windows). Streams the
## file in blocks, samples within each block, and parses only the kept rows so
## the raw text never accumulates.
sample_with_r <- function(path, p, keep_cols, block = 5e5) {
  con <- file(path, "r"); on.exit(close(con))
  hdr <- readLines(con, n = 1L)
  out <- list(); i <- 1L
  repeat {
    lns <- readLines(con, n = block)
    if (!length(lns)) break
    sel <- lns[runif(length(lns)) < p]
    if (length(sel)) {
      out[[i]] <- fread(
        text = c(hdr, sel), select = keep_cols,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE, showProgress = FALSE
      )
      i <- i + 1L
    }
  }
  res <- rbindlist(out, use.names = TRUE)
  chr <- names(res)[vapply(res, is.character, logical(1))]
  if (length(chr)) res[, (chr) := lapply(.SD, as.factor), .SDcols = chr]
  res[]
}

## Cheap and safe: only touches the CSV if it is actually reachable, so the
## report still knits from cache when the external drive is unplugged.
EST_ROWS <- tryCatch(estimate_total_rows(DATA_PATH), error = function(e) NA_real_)

cache_ok <- file.exists(CACHE_PATH) && !REFRESH_SAMPLE
if (cache_ok) {
  dat <- readRDS(CACHE_PATH)
  ## A cache drawn for a different GROUP_VAR won't have the column we need.
  if (!all(KEEP_COLS %in% names(dat))) {
    message("Cache is missing required columns - redrawing the sample.")
    cache_ok <- FALSE
  }
}

if (!cache_ok) {
  if (!file.exists(DATA_PATH)) {
    stop("Cannot find the data file at:\n  ", DATA_PATH,
         "\nIs the TOSHIBA EXT drive mounted?")
  }
  set.seed(SEED)
  est_rows <- estimate_total_rows(DATA_PATH)
  ## Oversample slightly so we land at or above SAMPLE_N, then trim exactly.
  p <- min(1, (SAMPLE_N / est_rows) * 1.03)
  message(sprintf("Estimated %s rows; sampling with p = %.4f ...",
                  format(est_rows, big.mark = ","), p))

  dat <- if (identical(SAMPLE_METHOD, "awk")) {
    sample_with_awk(DATA_PATH, p, KEEP_COLS, SEED)
  } else {
    sample_with_r(DATA_PATH, p, KEEP_COLS)
  }

  missing_cols <- setdiff(KEEP_COLS, names(dat))
  if (length(missing_cols)) {
    stop("These columns were not found in the CSV: ",
         paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  if (nrow(dat) > SAMPLE_N) dat <- dat[sample(.N, SAMPLE_N)]
  saveRDS(dat, CACHE_PATH, compress = FALSE)
  message(sprintf("Cached %s sampled rows to %s",
                  format(nrow(dat), big.mark = ","), CACHE_PATH))
}

setDF(dat)
dat[[GROUP_VAR]] <- as.character(dat[[GROUP_VAR]])
dat[[GROUP_VAR]][trimws(dat[[GROUP_VAR]]) == ""] <- NA_character_
```

```{r group-sizes}
group_sizes <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(.data[[GROUP_VAR]])) %>%
  count(group = .data[[GROUP_VAR]], name = "n_sampled") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_sampled)) %>%
  mutate(share = n_sampled / sum(n_sampled))

KEEP_GROUPS <- group_sizes$group[group_sizes$n_sampled >= MIN_GROUP_N]
DROPPED     <- setdiff(group_sizes$group, KEEP_GROUPS)
N_GROUPS    <- length(KEEP_GROUPS)

## Chart height scales with the number of groups, so the charts stay readable
## whether GROUP_VAR has 4 categories or 55.
FIG_HEIGHT <- max(4, min(22, 0.17 * N_GROUPS + 2.4))

if (SAVE_PNGS) dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## About this report

```{r overview, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
"Every chart below shows how one analysis variable is distributed across
values of **%s** (`%s`).

- **Source:** `%s`
- **Sample:** %s rows drawn at random from an estimated %s rows in the full
  file (about %.1f%%). Sampling is a single streaming pass, so no more than the
  sampled rows are ever held in memory. The draw is cached at
  `%s` &mdash; delete that file or set `REFRESH_SAMPLE <- TRUE` to redraw.
- **Groups shown:** %d of %d, after dropping any with fewer than %s sampled rows%s.
- **Chart types:** categorical variables are shown as 100%%-stacked bars
  (composition within each group); numeric variables as boxplots ordered by
  median, with outlier points suppressed and the axis zoomed to the %.1f&ndash;%.1f
  percentile range so long tails do not flatten the boxes.

Because these are sampled figures, treat small differences between groups as
noise. Percentages for the largest groups are accurate to well under a
percentage point; the smallest groups shown are considerably noisier.\n\n",
  GROUP_LABEL, GROUP_VAR,
  basename(DATA_PATH),
  format(nrow(dat), big.mark = ","),
  format(estimate_total_rows(DATA_PATH), big.mark = ","),
  100 * nrow(dat) / estimate_total_rows(DATA_PATH),
  basename(CACHE_PATH),
  N_GROUPS, nrow(group_sizes), format(MIN_GROUP_N, big.mark = ","),
  if (length(DROPPED)) paste0(" (dropped: ", paste(DROPPED, collapse = ", "), ")") else "",
  100 * TRIM_TAILS, 100 * (1 - TRIM_TAILS)
))
```

```{r type-table}
resolve_type <- function(var, column) {
  if (var %in% names(VAR_TYPES)) return(unname(VAR_TYPES[[var]]))
  if (is.numeric(column)) "numeric" else "categorical"
}

VAR_TYPE_RESOLVED <- vapply(
  ANALYSIS_VARS,
  function(v) resolve_type(v, dat[[v]]),
  character(1)
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Variable = ANALYSIS_VARS,
    Type     = VAR_TYPE_RESOLVED,
    Distinct = vapply(ANALYSIS_VARS,
                      function(v) format(length(unique(dat[[v]])), big.mark = ","),
                      character(1)),
    `Missing (%)` = vapply(ANALYSIS_VARS,
                           function(v) sprintf("%.2f", 100 * mean(is.na(dat[[v]]))),
                           character(1)),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  ),

)
```

<!-- ===================================================================== -->
<!--  3. PLOTTING FUNCTIONS                                                -->
<!--  Both take the grouping variable as an argument, so they work          -->
<!--  unchanged if GROUP_VAR is swapped out.                                -->
<!-- ===================================================================== -->

```{r plot-helpers}
x_labeller <- function(var) {
  if (var %in% DOLLAR_VARS) scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1, big.mark = ",")
  else scales::label_number(big.mark = ",", drop0trailing = TRUE)
}

## Put "Yes" before "No" so the stacked bars read the intuitive way.
tidy_levels <- function(f) {
  lv <- levels(f)
  if (setequal(setdiff(lv, "(Missing)"), c("Yes", "No"))) {
    lv <- c("Yes", "No", intersect("(Missing)", lv))
    f  <- factor(as.character(f), levels = lv)
  }
  f
}

## ---- Categorical: 100% stacked horizontal bars ------------------------
plot_categorical <- function(data, var, group_var, group_label) {
  d <- data %>%
    select(grp = all_of(group_var), val = all_of(var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(grp), grp %in% KEEP_GROUPS) %>%
    mutate(val = ifelse(is.na(as.character(val)), "(Missing)", as.character(val))) %>%
    mutate(val = tidy_levels(factor(val)))

  ## Reference level: "Yes" for binary variables, otherwise the most common
  ## level overall. Groups get sorted by its share, and it is placed first so
  ## it sits at the left edge of every bar where it is easiest to compare.
  ref <- if ("Yes" %in% levels(d$val)) "Yes" else {
    names(sort(table(d$val), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
  }
  by_freq  <- names(sort(table(d$val), decreasing = TRUE))
  lvl_ord  <- c(ref, setdiff(by_freq, c(ref, "(Missing)")))
  if ("(Missing)" %in% levels(d$val)) lvl_ord <- c(lvl_ord, "(Missing)")
  d$val <- factor(as.character(d$val), levels = lvl_ord)

  shares <- d %>%
    count(grp, val, name = "n") %>%
    group_by(grp) %>%
    mutate(share = n / sum(n), n_grp = sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup()

  ord <- shares %>%
    filter(val == ref) %>%
    arrange(share) %>%
    pull(grp)
  ord <- c(ord, setdiff(unique(shares$grp), ord))
  shares$grp <- factor(shares$grp, levels = ord)

  ## Keep the legend readable: long category names need fewer columns.
  lab_len  <- max(nchar(levels(shares$val)))
  leg_cols <- min(nlevels(shares$val),
                  if (lab_len > 30) 2 else if (lab_len > 18) 3 else 4)

  ggplot(shares, aes(x = share, y = grp, fill = val)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.78, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.005))) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.92, direction = -1) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = leg_cols, byrow = TRUE)) +
    labs(
      title    = var,
      subtitle = sprintf("Composition by %s, sorted by share \"%s\"",
                         tolower(group_label), ref),
      x        = "Share of sampled students",
      caption  = sprintf(
        "n = %s sampled students across %d %s groups; %d categories. Bars sum to 100%%.",
        format(sum(shares$n), big.mark = ","), length(unique(shares$grp)),
        tolower(group_label), nlevels(shares$val))
    )
}

## ---- Numeric: horizontal boxplots ordered by median -------------------
plot_numeric <- function(data, var, group_var, group_label) {
  d <- data %>%
    select(grp = all_of(group_var), val = all_of(var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(grp), grp %in% KEEP_GROUPS)

  n_all      <- nrow(d)
  pct_miss   <- 100 * mean(is.na(d$val))
  d          <- filter(d, !is.na(val))
  pct_zero   <- 100 * mean(d$val == 0)
  conditioned <- var %in% CONDITION_ON_POSITIVE
  if (conditioned) d <- filter(d, val > 0)

  if (!nrow(d) || length(unique(d$val)) < 2) {
    return(list(plot = NULL, note = sprintf(
      "*Not plotted: `%s` has no variation among the sampled rows%s.*",
      var, if (conditioned) " with a positive value" else "")))
  }

  med <- d %>%
    group_by(grp) %>%
    summarise(m = median(val), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(m)
  d$grp <- factor(d$grp, levels = med$grp)

  ## Zoom rather than filter: coord_cartesian keeps every row in the boxplot
  ## statistics and only clips the view. The window is the span of the drawn
  ## whiskers, tightened further if the TRIM_TAILS percentiles are narrower.
  ## Using the raw percentiles alone lets one very long tail (income, parent
  ## loans) squash every box flat against the axis.
  wh <- d %>%
    group_by(grp) %>%
    summarise(
      q1 = quantile(val, 0.25),
      q3 = quantile(val, 0.75),
      lo = min(val[val >= q1 - 1.5 * (q3 - q1)]),
      hi = max(val[val <= q3 + 1.5 * (q3 - q1)]),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  qt   <- unname(quantile(d$val, c(TRIM_TAILS, 1 - TRIM_TAILS), na.rm = TRUE))
  lims <- c(max(min(wh$lo), qt[1]), min(max(wh$hi), qt[2]))
  if (!all(is.finite(lims)) || lims[1] >= lims[2]) {
    lims <- range(d$val, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  lims <- lims + c(-1, 1) * diff(lims) * 0.02
  if (min(d$val, na.rm = TRUE) >= 0) lims[1] <- max(0, lims[1])

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = val, y = grp)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "#3B7EA1", colour = "grey25",
                 alpha = 0.85, linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.7) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = x_labeller(var)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = lims) +
    labs(
      title    = var,
      subtitle = sprintf("Distribution by %s, sorted by median%s",
                         tolower(group_label),
                         if (conditioned) " (positive values only)" else ""),
      x        = var,
      caption  = sprintf(paste0(
        "n = %s sampled students across %d %s groups. %.1f%% missing, ",
        "%.1f%% exactly zero%s.\n",
        "Boxes span the interquartile range; whiskers reach 1.5 x IQR; ",
        "outlier points suppressed.\n",
        "Axis clipped to %s-%s, so the extreme tail is not shown."),
        format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), length(unique(d$grp)),
        tolower(group_label), pct_miss, pct_zero,
        if (conditioned) "; zeros excluded" else "",
        x_labeller(var)(lims[1]), x_labeller(var)(lims[2]))
    )

  note <- if (!conditioned && pct_zero >= 40) sprintf(
    paste0("> **Note:** %.0f%% of sampled students have $0 for this variable, ",
           "so the boxes sit on or near zero. Add `\"%s\"` to ",
           "`CONDITION_ON_POSITIVE` in the config chunk to see the ",
           "distribution among recipients only."), pct_zero, var) else NULL

  list(plot = p, note = note)
}
```

# Distributions by `r tolower(GROUP_LABEL)`

```{r render-all, results='asis', fig.width=9, fig.height=FIG_HEIGHT}
for (v in ANALYSIS_VARS) {

  cat("\n\n## ", v, "\n\n", sep = "")

  if (identical(unname(VAR_TYPE_RESOLVED[[v]]), "numeric")) {
    res <- plot_numeric(dat, v, GROUP_VAR, GROUP_LABEL)
    p   <- res$plot
    if (is.null(p)) {
      cat(res$note, "\n\n")
      next
    }
    if (!is.null(res$note)) cat(res$note, "\n\n")
  } else {
    p <- plot_categorical(dat, v, GROUP_VAR, GROUP_LABEL)
  }

  print(p)
  cat("\n\n")

  if (SAVE_PNGS) {
    fname <- file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf(
      "%s-%s-by-%s.png", format(Sys.Date()),
      gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(v)), tolower(GROUP_VAR)))
    ggsave(fname, p, width = 9, height = FIG_HEIGHT, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
  }
}
```

# Reproducibility

```{r session, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
"- Sample seed: `%d`; sampling method: `%s`.\n
- Cached sample: `%s` (%s rows). Delete it or set `REFRESH_SAMPLE <- TRUE` to redraw.\n
- Note that `awk`'s random number generator is not identical across
  implementations, so the exact rows drawn may differ between machines. The
  cache file, not the seed, is what makes a specific set of figures
  reproducible &mdash; keep it if you need the numbers to stay fixed.\n\n",
  SEED, SAMPLE_METHOD, CACHE_PATH, format(nrow(dat), big.mark = ",")))
```
